cards.intuition: Rows are terms, columns are documents, and nonzero cells record occurrence. It is the clean mathematical model but mostly empty at corpus scale.
cards.formula: A(t,d)=1 if term t occurs in document d, else 0
cards.topic: Term-Document Incidence and Why Matrices Do Not Scale

cards.intuition: Do not store or scan millions of absences to find twenty presences. Keep only the document-column positions where the row is nonzero.
cards.topic: Term-Document Incidence and Why Matrices Do Not Scale

cards.intuition: Sparse terms favor ID lists; dense repeated filters can favor compressed bitmaps and machine-word intersections.
cards.formula: choose representation from density and operations
cards.topic: Term-Document Incidence and Why Matrices Do Not Scale

cards.intuition: The dictionary finds a normalized term and points to its ordered list of matching documents. Payloads add frequencies and positions.
cards.topic: The Inverted Index: Dictionary and Postings

cards.intuition: Document frequency counts containing documents; collection frequency counts every occurrence, including repetitions inside one document.
cards.formula: df(t)=number of containing docs; cf(t)=total occurrences
cards.topic: The Inverted Index: Dictionary and Postings

cards.intuition: Postings are a serving copy derived from authoritative content. Stable IDs, analyzer versions, checksums, and atomic publication make rebuilds safe.
cards.formula: source + analyzer version → versioned index artifact
cards.topic: The Inverted Index: Dictionary and Postings

cards.intuition: Walk two sorted lists, emit equal IDs, and advance whichever ID is smaller. Neither cursor moves backward.
cards.topic: Boolean Query Processing by Intersecting Postings

cards.intuition: OR merges sorted IDs while emitting either side once. NOT is best used to exclude from a positive candidate list, not to build the whole complement.
cards.formula: OR = sorted union; A AND NOT B = set difference
cards.topic: Boolean Query Processing by Intersecting Postings

cards.intuition: Document intersection proves all terms occur; positional comparison then proves they occur adjacently in the required order.
cards.formula: document AND first, positional constraint second
cards.topic: Boolean Query Processing by Intersecting Postings

cards.intuition: Begin AND processing with the shortest postings because intersections only shrink. Small early intermediates save later decoding and comparison.
cards.topic: Query Optimization: Processing Rarest Terms First

cards.concept: Document frequency as a cost estimate
cards.intuition: The dictionary already knows approximate postings length, giving the optimizer a cheap selectivity signal. Keep statistics aligned with the live index.
cards.topic: Query Optimization: Processing Rarest Terms First

cards.concept: Rarest-first is not the whole cost model
cards.intuition: Cache state, remote access, compression, skips, and operator semantics can outweigh a small cardinality difference. Selectivity is the starting estimate.
cards.formula: cost = cardinality × access and decode cost
cards.topic: Query Optimization: Processing Rarest Terms First
